subject: BridgeWorks connector: adapter strategy and POC milestones
messages:
From: Sofia Ramos <sofia@bridgeworks.ai>
To: diego_fernandez <diego@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 09 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intro + BridgeWorks -> Redwood connector exploration

Hi Diego —

Thanks again for the intro call yesterday. Lucas and I sketched a short project plan for a minimal connector between BridgeWorks' orchestration layer and Redwood's hosted runtime so our mutual customers can use BridgeWorks' pipeline UX with Redwood models and telemetry. High-level asks:

- lightweight SDK adapter (LangChain & LlamaIndex compatibility)
- trace hooks that map BridgeWorks spans to Redwood request ids
- a POC data flow that demonstrates streaming generation + function/tool calling

Attached is a one-pager with our POC requirements and a rough timeline. Can we get alignment on the scope and an internal owner at Redwood to unblock engineering? We're targeting a pilot with one joint customer in Q3.

Best,
Sofia Ramos
Head of Integrations, BridgeWorks
sofia@bridgeworks.ai
Attachment: bridgeworks-poc-requirements.pdf (pdf, 78KB)

From: diego_fernandez <diego@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia@bridgeworks.ai>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 09 May 2028 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + BridgeWorks -> Redwood connector exploration

Sofia —

Appreciate the succinct brief and the POC doc. Quick confirmation from our side: Redwood can commit an SDK adapter that exposes a connector layer with two integration points — runtime calls (generation/embedding) and tracing hooks. Proposed internal owners below and a recommended small-scope POC:

- Owner (Redwood): Diego (partner lead) + Vanessa (ISV engagement) + Marissa (runtime eng contact)
- Scope (minimal):
  - LangChain/LLamaIndex shim to translate BridgeWorks pipeline steps to Redwood API calls
  - Trace propagation: include redwood-request-id as span tag and emit an aggregate span on completion
  - Streaming + function call demo using a sample ingestion pipeline (no customer data)

Open questions for you:
1) Do you prefer the adapter to be published as an NPM/PyPI package or maintained in a joint GitHub repo under BridgeWorks org?
2) For tracing, do you need OpenTelemetry context forwarding or just a correlation id mapping?

I'll circulate a one-page adapter proposal with cost/time estimates by EOD. Can you confirm Lucas will be our technical reviewer?

- Diego
Diego Fernandez
Partner Solutions, Redwood Inference
Attachment: adapter-proposal-v1.docx (docx, 42KB)

From: Lucas Zheng <lucas@bridgeworks.ai>
To: diego_fernandez <diego@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sofia Ramos <sofia@bridgeworks.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 09 May 2028 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + BridgeWorks -> Redwood connector exploration

On Wed, May 9, 2028 at 10:04 AM diego_fernandez <diego@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Sofia —
> 
> Appreciate the succinct brief and the POC doc. Quick confirmation from our side: Redwood can commit an SDK adapter that exposes a connector layer with two integration points — runtime calls (generation/embedding) and tracing hooks. Proposed internal owners below and a recommended small-scope POC:
> 
> - Owner (Redwood): Diego (partner lead) + Vanessa (ISV engagement) + Marissa (runtime eng contact)

Thanks Diego — that owner list looks good. To answer your questions:

1) We prefer the adapter live under BridgeWorks' org as a canonical integration (we'll mirror to our internal registries as needed). BridgeWorks will take release responsibility for the first 3 months, then we can discuss co-maintenance.
2) Tracing: we want OpenTelemetry context forwarding so that customers can see an end-to-end trace in their preferred APM. Correlation ids alone won't cut it for our SRE customers.

Two asks from our engineering side:
- Can Redwood include an example of KV cache-aware calls (we have bursty conversational workloads) so we can validate token-level cost impact?
- For streaming, we'd like a minimal example that demonstrates partial outputs + function call responses (to validate UX in BridgeWorks' pipeline viewer).

I'll schedule a short technical sync with Karthik for tomorrow if that works.

— Lucas
Lucas Zheng
Senior Platform Engineer, BridgeWorks
Attachment: (none)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lucas Zheng <lucas@bridgeworks.ai>, diego_fernandez <diego@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 09 May 2028 16:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + BridgeWorks -> Redwood connector exploration

Thanks Lucas — that schedule works for me. A few pragmatic decisions from our runtime team to keep the POC narrow and deliverable in 4 weeks:

- We'll implement the adapter as a small Python package in the BridgeWorks org (pyproject + wheel). We'll provide a companion TypeScript example for LangChain users.
- Tracing: Redwood will emit OTLP spans and accept incoming context via standard W3C traceparent/header propagation; we'll add a middleware shim to translate to redwood-request-id for correlation in our logs.
- KV cache example: we'll prepare a short script that shows hit/miss metrics and token delta for a sample conversational session.
- Streaming + function calls: we'll include a demo that triggers a function call, streams partial tokens, and then emits a final payload — this will be used in your pipeline viewer.

Next steps: Diego to update the HubSpot deal with scope & timeline -> Link: https://hubspot.company.com/deal/BW-4921; Vanessa to own docs + external comms; Marissa will spin up a small sandbox cluster for testing.

If no objections, I'll send a calendar invite for the technical sync.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Engineer, Runtime Integrations, Redwood Inference
